name: Bears Repeating
sources: LP1 3:31:08-3:36:40 (archive.org PS4 longplay Part 1; frames every 1-2 s at 854x480; HUD crops; exit crate sign)
gamepressure.com Bears Repeating walkthrough (enemy/hazard corroboration; its '137 boxes' is wrong, the HUD shows /227)
camera: mixed: into-screen snowfield, toward-camera rope-bridge run, side-view cavern/slow-mo area and bonus, chase camera behind the bear
typesNote: Crash 4 keys: wood, question, bounceWumpa (crate with a gold wumpa emblem), arrowWood, reinforced (metal-banded strong crate), tnt, nitro (counted when exploded; the exit Nitro switch pays any still standing), checkpoint, unknown. Not counted: metal ! boxes (including the bonus's floating timed !), iron arrow crates (the 6-wide wall on the ride and 3 on the bonus tower), outline/iron lid blocks.

routes.basis: 227 minus bonus 27; includes 36 + 8 slow-mo Nitro and 13 Nitro paid by the exit switch
yellow-gem path (needs a gem from another level) not taken in the LP; the ALL gem was still awarded

sections.notes: GR 46; HUD 1/227 (LP1 3:31:18) and 3/227 (3:31:21). Snowfield with robot drones, plank lake, cable-car platforms carrying crate columns.

sections.to: arrow crate by the red lantern
sections.notes: GR 62. TNT stacks on hanging platforms, scaffold towers; the hidden-gem drop is beside the arrow crate.
GR 70 (GR calls it a 'yellow gem bonus room'; the LP shows ordinary main-route crates on the spinning discs, a toward-camera rope bridge, bumper pads and a cave).
GR 80; C2 at LP1 3:33:18; side-view scaffold room with a TNT under two crates.
GR 82/97/133. Side-view ice cavern; a Nitro row ending in one crate; a giant Nitro block detonated in slow-mo (+36).
GR 136: C3 (LP1 3:34:14) + 2 crates by the pad.
HUD 0/27 (LP1 3:34:20) -> 27/27 (3:34:55); main 163/227 (3:34:59-3:35:04). Timed ! closes an outline lid over the crate row.
GR 204 before the checkpoint; HUD 205/227 at LP1 3:36:06 just after it. Forced-speed polar-bear ride, toward the camera's back.
Exit crate sign 214/227 (LP1 3:36:27). Lighter half, seeded with Nitro.
Nitro switch in front of the sign pays 13 Nitro (214 -> 227).

puzzles.summary: TNT beside two floating crates at the start.
puzzles.solution: Stomp the TNT and back off; the blast breaks the two floating crates.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Standing next to it, or trying to jump for the floating pair first.
puzzles.loss: A life, or 2 crates if the TNT is set off from too far away.

puzzles.summary: Three TNT stacks in two minutes: TNT on top of wood, strong crate on top of TNT on a moving platform, TNT under two crates.
puzzles.solution: S2-b: spin the base, step back. S2-c: light the TNT and leave the platform, so the blast opens the strong crate. S4-e: take the upper pair first.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Body-slamming onto S2-c's strong crate with the TNT below; lighting S4-e before the pair is taken (the blast still takes them, but on a ledge you may be caught).
puzzles.loss: A life (on hanging platforms the safe zone is small).

puzzles.summary: Slow-mo explosives: a Nitro row ending in a crate, then a giant Nitro block.
puzzles.solution: Break the end crate in slow-mo and get clear. For the block, set it off in slow-mo, jump past, cancel slow-mo as it goes.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Running past without detonating (the Nitros stay standing).
puzzles.loss: Not lost: Nitros left standing appear to be paid by the exit switch only if still present. LP: the row and block were detonated (+44 by GR).

puzzles.summary: Bonus: a floating timed ! starts a countdown after which a long outline row over the dock crates turns to iron.
puzzles.solution: Hit the ! with slow-mo active, detonate the Nitro bridge, sweep the dock row under the lid, then take the floating pair (Nitro under slow-mo).
puzzles.wrongOrder: Hitting the ! without slow-mo, or crossing the Nitro bridge.
puzzles.loss: Bonus crates: once the lid is iron the remaining dock crates are sealed (the round restarts on death).

puzzles.summary: Bear ride first half: 41 crates before the bear checkpoint with no counter on screen.
puzzles.solution: Memorise lanes: hit 2-stacks with a jump at the lip, hug the left wall in the cavern, don't over-steer while the camera swings.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Steering at every crate (over-correction drops the next lane), passing the checkpoint after a miss.
puzzles.loss: All-box only: a missed crate means dying and retrying before the checkpoint (GR).

puzzles.solution: Press the green ! in front of the sign (214/227).

observations: Four acts: on-foot snowfield and caverns (80 crates in about 2 min), a slow-mo explosives set piece (53, of which 44 are Nitro), a 27-crate bonus, and the bear ride (51 crates plus 13 Nitro credited at the exit).

Hazards are box credit: about 64 of the 227 boxes are Nitro (row 8, block 36, bonus 7, exit switch 13), plus at least 7 TNT. One slow-mo detonation of the giant block is worth 36 crates, 16 % of the level.
Cable-car platforms carry tall columns and blocks (S1-j, S1-k): many crates per landing, on a footing that is moving, so the player commits to a stomp chain.
TNT stacking is varied rather than repeated: TNT next to floating crates (tool), TNT on top of wood, a strong crate on top of TNT, TNT under a crate pair. Four variants in three minutes.

The bear ride's first half holds 41 crates and the HUD never shows; it is designed for memorisation (GR: die and retry before the checkpoint). Crates sit in left/centre/right lanes, 2-stacks are centred on lips where a JUMP prompt appears, and two crates hide behind ice pillars against the left wall.
The second half is light (9 crates) and seeded with Nitro: the ride turns from collecting to dodging, and the dodged Nitro are paid by the exit switch, so dodging never costs the box gem.
A full-width wall of 6 iron arrow crates on a rise is terrain, not a collectible: a forced launch gate on a vehicle section.
Rope-bridge and bumper stretches use one crate per post (S3), spacing pickups to the rhythm of the posts rather than clustering them.
The yellow-gem plate shows a hint banner without the key; the run had no yellow gem yet earned ALL, so that path carries no counted crates.
Checkpoints sit at 46, ≈ 71, 134 and 205: the front-loaded C1 follows the densest on-foot stretch, and the bear checkpoint locks in the hardest all-box segment.
The hidden gem is marked by a red lantern beside the arrow crate: a light as a visual tell for a drop.

cameraSections.notes: Snowy canyon from the spawn, fenced downhill path and plank lake (LP1 3:31:12–3:31:40); ice cave with hanging platforms up to C1 (3:31:41–3:31:54).
Ice cave with hanging pads, a hand-over-hand pipe frame and steel scaffolds to the arrow-crate walkway (3:31:54–3:32:20).

Chasm with rod-hung pads and lift discs (3:32:22–3:32:30); a disc lowers Crash from the drill tower and the camera turns to face him for the rope-bridge run back toward the camera (3:32:32–3:33:00); a disc lifts him into a dark cave (3:33:02–3:33:14).
Snow path with C2 and machinery walkways (3:33:16–3:33:26); side-view scaffold room (3:33:28–3:33:32).
Side-scrolling ice cavern: hanging pads, rope-strung ice slabs, tipping pads, the Nitro row and the giant Nitro block (3:33:33–3:34:08).
Steel blocks over gas vents to C3 and the bonus pad (3:34:10–3:34:18).
Forced downhill run; the camera swings at bends while the line stays fairly straight (GR); BOOST and JUMP prompts (3:35:07–3:36:07).
Second half after the bear checkpoint, with Cortex's blimp overhead (3:36:07–3:36:25).
End platform with the crate sign and the Nitro switch (3:36:27–3:36:29).

geometryObservations: Four camera grammars carry four platform grammars. On foot, into-screen: small gaps over water and chasms. Slow-mo cavern, side view: moving footing hung from the ceiling. Bonus, side view: a timed slot. Bear, chase camera: lanes, with almost no gaps.

Hanging footing is the on-foot theme, in strict escalation. Static rafts (P-S1-c), then hung pads and decks (S1-S2), then lift discs that carry you vertically (S3), then crumbling slabs and tipping pads under slow-mo (S5), then the bear, where the footing is forced.

Decks carry crates; pads carry none. The 1.5-2 u pads are pure stepping stones; every crate group sits on a 3x3 u or larger deck (columns, 3x2 block, 2x2 ? block). Collecting never happens on the smallest footing.

The drone owner is a protected-projectile archetype, taught in four steps. Open floor (E-S1-a), then across a raft gap (E-S1-b), then hovering inside the gaps between pads (E-S3-a), then hurdles on a narrow toward-camera bridge (E-S3-c). The counter (hit the owner) never changes; the geometry around it does.

Camera reversal is used as difficulty. The rope bridge is run toward the camera on a 2.5 u deck with drone pairs, so depth (gap and drone distance) is read late. That is why the bridge has railed rope sides and posts every 6-8 u as rests.

The mask arrives exactly at the crumble run. Slow-mo is first used on rope-strung ice slabs (3:33:37), the archetypal timing gap, and only later on the Nitro set pieces. The tool is taught on footing before it is used on explosives.

Explosive set pieces are built as gaps. The giant Nitro block sits beside 2-3 u steel blocks with ~2 u gaps (P-S5-g), so the explosion is a moving hazard you traverse beside, not a wall in front of you.

Rest spacing on foot: a railed scaffold rest or wide deck every 3-4 jumps in the cavern (P-S5-b), and checkpoints on solid ground above or after each hanging stretch (C1 above the block deck, C2 on a snow path, C3 after the steel blocks).

The bonus is a geometry timer. The crate row fills a slot exactly one crate high under an outline row that turns to iron. The sweep is run along the crate tops inside that slot, and the closed lid becomes the bridge to the exit.

Bear-lane grammar: the valley is 10-14 u wide, with corridors and tunnels of ~5-6 u. Hazards (trees, rocks, pillars, a hole, skiers) take one lane at a time and alternate sides, and the crates sit in the free lane, often right beside the hazard.

Bear jumps are few and announced. Two ravines and a ridge (with a JUMP prompt and a 2-stack on the lip), plus one forced launch off a full-width wall of iron arrow crates. Everything else is steering.

The second half swaps enemies for mines. Nitro pairs, a diagonal weave and fences replace skiers, and the dodged Nitro are paid at the exit, so the geometry tests steering without costing the box gem.

Height on foot is double-jump scale. Scaffold risers are ~2 u with fruit columns marking the jumps (P-S2-f, P-S4-d); the hand-over-hand pipe frame (P-S2-d) and the lift discs are the only non-jump traversals.
geometryTransfer: Protected projectile: pair a `sentry` (or two `floater`s) with a `grunt` owner and switch them off when the owner dies. Teach it on a 10-12 u (11-14 m) open floor first, then put the same pair across a 2-3 u water `pit`, then hover `floater`s in the 2.3-3.5 m gaps between `mover` pads.

Lift discs map to vertical `mover` platforms about 2 u (2.3 m) across. Use them to move between a lower walkway and a raised grind line, since a skater cannot climb 4-6 m any other way. A slow spin is cosmetic; keep the rider's facing stable.

Crumble run without slow-mo: four `crumble` slabs about 2x1 u (2.3x1.2 m), 2-3 u (2.3-3.5 m) apart, which a 9 m/s runner crosses at about one slab per 0.35 s, with a ≥ 0.5 s collapse delay and a railed scaffold `platform` rest after them. Follow it with `spinbridge` tipping pads at the same spacing.

Bear lanes as a skate downhill: a 12-16 m wide `terrain` slope with three lanes. Put one lane hazard (a tree prop, a `stone`, or a 1.7 m `pit` hole) every 25-35 m, alternating lanes, with a crate in the free lane beside it. Use a full-width `trampoline` row on a rise as the forced launch, and prompt only two ravine ollies.

Giant Nitro block as a traversal hazard: place a 7x3x3 Nitro block beside a line of 2-3 u `platform` blocks with ~2 u gaps, and start the chain from a TNT at the near end (3 s fuse). The blast front (≈ 7.9 m/s) is slower than a 9 m/s runner, so a player who lights it and keeps hopping outruns it.

One-crate slot under a ceiling: a crate row on a pier under a solid ceiling one crate (1.15 m) above it. The board cannot ollie over the row (1.7 m apex hits the ceiling), so the only clean line is grinding the row, which breaks it (≥ 6.5 m/s if TNT is mixed in).
